#### What this PR does / why we need it:

1. Add a `VolumeMounts` label: `io.kubernetes.container.volumeMounts`
2. Use this to populate `containerStatus.volumeMounts`

This is prework for [dynamic node-local ephemeral volumes](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6395). 

Today the CRI `Mount` does *not* store the volume name or subpath. Kubelet works around this by copying podSpec fields into `containerStatuses.volumeMounts`, and then assuming they are immutable for the rest of the pod lifecycle. This assumption will break with dynamic containers and dynamic volumes.

Inspired by the pattern of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143359, this PR serializes the container's `volumeMounts` into a CRI container annotation to use for bookkeeping. Then, the kubelet can compute `containerStatuses.volumeMounts` directly from the runtime container's status. 

An alternative could be for Kubelet to checkpoint the volumeMount status into its actuation checkpoint, but the mechanism proposed in this PR feels cleaner and less complex. This PR also has synergy with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143359; using the CRI allows us to populate `volumeMounts` in the container statuses for missing containers not in the podspec.

Terminated / exited containers retain their `containerStatuses.volumeMounts` entries until the pod itself is deleted and garabage-collected, preserving today's behavior.

body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This is prework for Dynamic Node-Local Ephemeral Volumes ([KEP-6395](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6395)).

Kubelet currently has an actuated pod state that is written to a local checkpoint file to survive pod restarts. This actuated state exists to support dynamic pod operations that are supported today including in-place pod resize, dynamic containers, and dynamic empty-dir volume resize.

This PR checkpoints mounted inline pod volumes into the kubelet's actuated pod state when volumes are mounted in `ActualStateOfWorld`, removes them when unmounted, and uses the checkpointed volume specs during `VolumeManager` reconciler reconstruction on kubelet restart.

Previously, volume reconstruction on kubelet startup relied solely on scanning pod volume directories on disk via `ConstructVolumeSpec`, which could only construct stub `v1.Volume` specs (missing fields such as `ConfigMap.Name`, `EmptyDir.Medium`/`SizeLimit`, `Projected.Sources`, etc.) until the pod spec was re-synced into `DesiredStateOfWorld`. Recording mounted volumes in `actuatedState` allows the `VolumeManager` reconciler to reconstruct the full `v1.Volume` spec and pod metadata directly from the actuation checkpoint, including for volumes that may later be removed from `pod.Spec.Volumes` while still mounted on disk.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6395

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Structured in 3 commits for easier review:
1. `kubelet/state`: add `GetPodVolumes`, `SetPodVolume`, and `RemovePodVolume` to `allocation/state`.
2. `volumemanager`: record mounted volumes in `actuatedState` from `ActualStateOfWorld` and reconstruct volume specs from `actuatedState` in the reconciler.
3. `kubelet`: share the `actuatedState` checkpoint instance between `kuberuntime` and `VolumeManager`, and preserve checkpointed volumes when `InitializeActuatedPod` runs.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. AI wrote the code (based on my design), I reviewed, edited, & tested it.

/sig node
/sig storage
/assign @tallclair @msau42
title: kubelet: checkpoint pod volumes into actuated state, and use it for ASOW reconstruction

body:
This PR updates API of storage health as per - https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1432

It also moves health from pod to `pod.Status.Volumestatus` as discussed in - https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6395 

Here is brief summary of what it does:

1. It moves `volumeHealth` from `pod.Status` to `pod.Status.VolumeStatus` 
2. It adds `Unknown` and `Healthy` enum values to core pvc/pod health types. The idea is - we should be able to report healthy volumes if driver reports no adverse conditions and absorb any unknown conditions in `Unknown`.
3. It adds similar `Uknown` and `Healthy` enum values to storage/CSINOde type.
4. It makes it clear that - both enum can take new values and what should be the behaviour of the reader and writer when this happens.




```release-note
Add support for Unknown and Healthy Volumes in Health APIs
```
title: Update volume health APIs as per newest version of KEP

#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR has the following dependencies:
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143474

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Note that we decided to remove the mutable mounts portion of this PR, deferring that to the next cycle.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Added alpha support for dynamically adding and removing node-local ephemeral volumes.
* The following volume types are supported: `emptyDir`, `configMap`, `secret`, `projected`, `image`.
* You may add and remove these volume types under the `/dynamic`subresource behind the `DynamicNodeLocalEphemeralVolumes` feature gate.
* To use newly added volumes, you must use the `DynamicContainers` feature to add a container referencing the new volume. In this first alpha, dynamically adjusting `volumeMounts` of a preexisting container is not yet allowed.
```
